analyses.name: Terreno Realty Corporation
analyses.verdict: The best-built base in a 524-name universe — a coastal infill industrial REIT with 40% earnings growth that is still 4% below its high while the rest of the leadership group is overbought.

financials.summary: Terreno is a pure-play owner of infill industrial property in six coastal US markets — Northern New Jersey/New York, Los Angeles, Miami, Seattle, San Francisco Bay Area and Washington DC. The model is deliberately narrow: buy functionally obsolete or under-rented last-mile warehouses inside supply-constrained submarkets, re-lease at market, and fund growth with equity rather than leverage. That produces an unusually clean income statement for a REIT — low debt cost, very high same-store cash re-leasing spreads, and FFO per share that compounds off rent roll-ups rather than acquisition volume. FY2025 continued that pattern: revenue grew low-double-digits as expiring leases reset materially higher, and the balance sheet stayed one of the least levered in the sector, which is why rising long-end Treasury yields have hurt Terreno's multiple far less than they have hurt levered net-lease peers. The scan's trailing figures show revenue +12.7% and EPS +40.2% year over year — the earnings line growing more than three times faster than the top line, which is the signature of re-leasing spreads dropping straight to the bottom line.
highlights: Revenue +12.7% YoY — driven by cash re-leasing spreads, not acquisition growth
EPS +40.2% YoY — earnings growing 3x faster than revenue
Occupancy has consistently run in the mid-to-high 90s across the six coastal markets
Among the lowest-levered balance sheets in the industrial REIT group — equity-funded growth
Forward P/E 41.2 (price/FFO basis is far lower — the P/E optic overstates the valuation for a REIT)

accomplishments: Sustained double-digit cash re-leasing spreads on expiring leases through 2025 and into 2026
Continued to raise the dividend annually, funded from growing FFO rather than leverage
Kept the six-market discipline while peers diversified into secondary markets that are now over-supplied
Held occupancy in the mid-90s through the 2024-25 national industrial supply wave that hit Sun Belt landlords hardest
Reached an all-time high share price at 75.08 within the last 52 weeks

journey_52w.summary: A one-way grind higher from 51.24 to 75.08 — roughly +47% at the peak — followed by a controlled three-contraction consolidation that has held the rising 50-DMA the whole way. The stock did not participate in the 2025 AI melt-up, which is precisely why it is not participating in the 2026 AI unwind. Over the past quarter it added 11.6% while the S&P slipped below its 50-DMA, and its relative strength line printed a new high even as price stayed 4.4% below its own.

analyses.name: Assurant, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A stock at all-time highs with an RSI of 53 and a 2.5% tightest contraction — the definition of a leader resting, at 12.5x earnings that grew 91%.

financials.summary: Assurant is not a conventional insurer. Its two engines are Global Lifestyle — mobile device protection programmes sold through carriers and retailers, plus vehicle service contracts — and Global Housing, which is dominated by lender-placed homeowners insurance. Both are fee-and-service businesses embedded in someone else's distribution, which makes revenue unusually sticky and capital requirements unusually light for the earnings produced. FY2025 was a strong year on both sides: Global Housing benefited from firm lender-placed pricing and a comparatively benign catastrophe load relative to reserves, while Global Lifestyle continued converting connected-device subscriber growth into fee income. The trailing figures in the scan show revenue +11.3% and EPS +91.2% — a near-doubling of earnings on low-double-digit revenue growth, which tells you this was a margin and loss-ratio year, amplified by an aggressive buyback that has been shrinking the share count for several years running.

analyses.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
analyses.verdict: 8.1x forward earnings with revenue up 23.5% — the cheapest quality name in the market's leading sector, and rising yields are a tailwind rather than a threat.

financials.summary: RGA is one of the world's largest life and health reinsurers. It earns money two ways that both currently work: underwriting margin on mortality, morbidity and longevity risk ceded by primary insurers, and investment income on a very large float. The second engine is why RGA is a beneficiary of the exact macro condition that is breaking growth stocks — the Treasury sell-off that is compressing tech multiples raises the reinvestment yield on RGA's bond portfolio, and because reinsurance liabilities are long-dated, higher rates lift book value economics over time. FY2025 also benefited from continued strength in the pension risk transfer and asset-intensive reinsurance markets, where RGA has been a leading counterparty for insurers seeking to offload longevity and annuity blocks. The scan's trailing data shows revenue +23.5% and EPS +16.6% — top-line growth outpacing earnings, which for a reinsurer usually signals aggressive new-business volume being written at acceptable but not spectacular margins.

Forward P/E 8.1 — the cheapest multiple among the scan's A-grade leaders

analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: The liquid, institution-grade way to own this rotation, and the only mega-cap leader with zero earnings risk for 75 days.

financials.summary: JPMorgan is the most diversified large financial in the world and FY2025 demonstrated why that matters: net interest income stayed elevated as the Fed held rates higher for longer, while the capital-markets side — trading, debt and equity underwriting, and advisory — reaccelerated sharply from the depressed 2023-24 base. Asset and wealth management continued to compound fee income off record client assets. Credit costs normalised but stayed manageable, with card charge-offs rising from unsustainably low levels rather than deteriorating outright. Consumer deposits proved stickier than the 2023 regional-bank crisis had implied, and the balance sheet ended the year with a substantial CET1 buffer above requirements, which is what has funded the buyback. The scan's trailing figures show revenue +30.4% and EPS +46.9% — capital-markets recovery plus rate-driven NII, amplified by share count reduction.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: The cleanest mega-cap chart in the market: +42% in a quarter with RSI at 48.5 — a $1.08T stock that went up and then fully reset without giving anything back.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the year the incretin franchise moved from launch to scale. Mounjaro (tirzepatide, type 2 diabetes) and Zepbound (the obesity indication) drove the overwhelming majority of Lilly's growth, with manufacturing capacity — not demand — remaining the binding constraint through most of the year as the company brought new fill-finish and API sites online. Gross margins expanded as production scaled, and operating leverage was dramatic: revenue growth in the mid-50s translated into earnings growth well over 100% because the incremental unit carried a far higher margin than the legacy portfolio. Alongside the incretins, Verzenio in oncology and the newer Alzheimer's asset contributed, while older diabetes products continued to decline. R&D spend stayed heavy, funding oral GLP-1 development and next-generation combination candidates. The scan's trailing figures show revenue +55.5% and EPS +169.9% — the most extreme operating-leverage combination of any mega-cap in this universe.

analyses.name: Liquidia Corporation
analyses.verdict: The highest-momentum name in the market that still has a clean chart — revenue up more than 40x on the Yutrepia launch, and RSI is only 55.9 after a +128% quarter.

financials.summary: Liquidia is a commercial-stage company built around one asset: Yutrepia, a dry-powder inhaled treprostinil for pulmonary arterial hypertension and PH-ILD, delivered via the company's PRINT particle-engineering platform. FY2025 was the transition year from a development-stage cost centre to a revenue-generating commercial business — which is why the growth rates look absurd. The scan shows revenue up more than 40x year over year, because the comparison base was essentially pre-commercial. What matters operationally is that the launch trajectory has been strong: prescriber uptake, payer coverage and refill persistence have all moved in the right direction, and the dry-powder format is a genuine convenience advantage over nebulised alternatives for PAH patients. The company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis while it funds the commercial build-out, so the forward P/E of 14.9 reflects expected rather than realised earnings. The balance sheet is the key fundamental question — cash runway versus the pace of commercial spend.

analyses.name: Datadog, Inc.
analyses.verdict: TradingView's most emphatic rating in the entire file (17 buy / 1 sell) on a stock that rose 97% in a quarter and reset RSI to 47 — the best software setup in a market selling software.

financials.summary: Datadog sells observability — infrastructure monitoring, APM, log management, security monitoring and, increasingly, LLM observability — as a consumption-based cloud platform. FY2025 was a strong year on both the growth and profitability axes. Revenue grew in the low-to-mid 30s as customers expanded product adoption (the multi-product attach rate has been the core compounding mechanism), and the AI-native customer cohort became a visibly material contributor as model-serving workloads generated exactly the kind of high-volume telemetry Datadog charges for. Critically, margin expansion accelerated: non-GAAP operating margin improved materially and free cash flow conversion stayed high, which is what produced earnings growth roughly 3x the revenue growth rate. The scan shows revenue +32.2% and EPS +104.0%. The structural point that explains why DDOG is holding while NVDA and VRT break: observability is the *operating cost* of running AI, billed monthly on consumption, not the capital expenditure of building it.

analyses.name: NetApp, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The one piece of enterprise infrastructure that isn't being liquidated: +60% in a quarter, RSI 51.7, 17.6x forward, and no earnings for 35 days.

financials.summary: NetApp runs on an April fiscal year, so its most recent full year captures the period in which enterprise storage was re-rated as an AI-adjacent business rather than a legacy one. The company's growth engine is all-flash array revenue plus public-cloud storage services (its first-party offerings on the major hyperscalers), while the older hybrid and hardware-maintenance base declines. FY2026 was a good year on both counts: all-flash and cloud storage services grew, gross margin held up on a favourable product mix, and disciplined operating expense control converted that into faster earnings growth. The AI angle is real but specific — training and inference workloads require high-throughput, low-latency data pipelines, and NetApp's ONTAP data-management layer sits in a defensible position for enterprises that want AI on their own governed data. The scan shows revenue +12.5% and EPS +23.4%: modest top-line growth converted into roughly double the earnings growth through mix and cost discipline. At 17.6x forward, it is priced as a legacy hardware vendor while performing as an AI-data-infrastructure company.

analyses.name: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners PLC
analyses.verdict: A defensive bottler acting like a growth stock — EPS +68%, volume at 1.87x average into a 3.1% coil, and TradingView at 16 buy / 1 sell.

financials.summary: CCEP is the largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue, with franchise territories spanning Western Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia and the Pacific. The business model is volume times price times mix, less a largely fixed manufacturing and distribution cost base — so small changes in realised price/mix produce large changes in operating profit. FY2025 was almost entirely a price/mix and margin year rather than a volume year: revenue was essentially flat (+0.2% in the scan's trailing data) while EPS grew 68.3%. That gap is explained by revenue-per-case management, favourable pack and channel mix, easing input and freight costs versus the prior year, and the continued integration and margin normalisation of the Asia Pacific territories. The Indonesian operation remains the long-duration growth option — a very large, low-per-capita-consumption market. Free cash flow conversion has been strong and the company has been steadily deleveraging while raising the dividend.

analyses.name: Apple Inc.
analyses.verdict: The strongest mega-cap tech chart in the market — and it reports tomorrow, which is the only reason this is WATCH and not a buy.

financials.summary: Apple's fiscal year ends in late September. FY2025 was a reacceleration year after a flat FY2024: iPhone returned to growth on a strong upgrade cycle, and Services — the App Store, iCloud, advertising, payments, and the Google search arrangement — continued to compound at a materially higher gross margin than hardware, which is why total company gross margin kept drifting upward. Mac and iPad grew off easy comparisons on the back of the Apple silicon refresh cycle, while Wearables remained the soft spot. Geographically, Greater China stayed the contested region. The capital return programme remained the largest in corporate history, with buybacks meaningfully reducing the share count and flattering EPS growth relative to net income growth. Notably, Apple's AI strategy has been on-device and partnership-led rather than capex-led — it is not building hyperscale training clusters — which is precisely why its cash flows are not exposed to the AI-infrastructure unwind now breaking NVDA, VRT, ALAB and ORCL. The scan's trailing data shows revenue +16.6% and EPS +21.8%, with the gap accounted for by margin mix and buyback.
